name: Guillaume Lample
milestone_by_age_26: In March 2016 at age 25, first-authored the NAACL 2016 paper Neural Architectures for Named Entity Recognition (BiLSTM-CRF NER), a highly cited SOTA result while at Carnegie Mellon.
early_history_summary: Born 8 October 1990 in Brest, France; prep maths at Lycée Kerichen then École Polytechnique (X2011). Master’s-level AI work at Carnegie Mellon with Chris Dyer produced the 2016 NER paper; later PhD on unsupervised machine translation (Sorbonne/Meta, 2016–2019), FAIR/Meta LLaMA work, then co-founded Mistral AI (2023) as Chief Science Officer.
family_context_summary: Raised in Brest; father Guy-Dominique Lample is a maxillofacial surgeon; sister Judith is an anesthesiologist in the same Brest clinic—professional medical household, not a tech dynasty.
parent_family_domain_summary: Parents/siblings are medical professionals; no documented AI/software domain apprenticeship.
primary_early_advantage_tags: École Polytechnique, CMU NLP, FAIR/Meta, French prépa pipeline, medical professional family, chess competition culture
evidence_summary: Birth date and Brest origins corroborated by French regional press; NAACL 2016 NER first-authorship dated on arXiv (Mar 2016) at age 25 with 6000+ citations; second sources (ACL Anthology, Scholar, Le Télégramme, Mistral/École Polytechnique pages) confirm Polytechnique→CMU→Meta→Mistral path. Family medical status documented; no inherited tech capital. Later unsupervised MT, LLaMA, and Mistral founding amplify tier-2 AI-founder status.
starting_point: Born 1990 in Brest, France, to a medical professional family (father maxillofacial surgeon); competitive prépa then elite Polytechnique track.
current_position: Co-founder and Chief Science Officer of Mistral AI (Paris); reported billionaire stake from Mistral valuation; lives/works in France.

trajectory.event: Admitted to École Polytechnique (X2011) after Kerichen prépa in Brest.
First-authored NAACL 2016 Neural Architectures for Named Entity Recognition while at CMU—widely cited BiLSTM-CRF NER work.
Published influential unsupervised machine translation and word translation papers (ICLR/EMNLP era) during Meta/Sorbonne PhD.
Defended PhD on unsupervised machine translation; continued as FAIR/Meta research scientist in Paris.
Co-authored Meta LLaMA work and co-founded Mistral AI with Arthur Mensch and Timothée Lacroix as Chief Science Officer.
Mistral scaled to multi-billion valuation; Lample among France’s first AI-founder billionaires per Bloomberg/Forbes profiles.

name: Hans Peter Brondmo
milestone_by_age_26: In 1987 at about age 24–25, after MIT undergrad, co-founded Snappy Software (expert systems) with seed funding from Apple Computer; by 1988 (age 26) joined Apple on HyperCard development in Japan.
early_history_summary: Born 22 June 1962 in Waterville, Maine; raised outside Hønefoss, Norway; Norwegian military service then MIT CS, CERN research internship, MIT Media Lab Interactive Cinema (micons/motion icons). Early founder (Snappy Software 1987), Apple HyperCard engineer, then DIVA/VideoShop (Media Lab spin-off, later Avid), email marketing (Post Communications), Plum (sold to Nokia), and later Google X Everyday Robots VP.
family_context_summary: Born in Maine, raised in Norway near Hønefoss; detailed parental occupations and wealth not documented in reviewed sources.
primary_early_advantage_tags: MIT CS, Media Lab Interactive Cinema, Apple seed funding, HyperCard, CERN internship, Cambridge MA tech cluster
evidence_summary: Wikipedia gives birth date 22 June 1962 and documents Snappy Software co-founding in 1987 with Apple seed funding plus 1988 Apple HyperCard role—both at or before age 26. Second sources (Techonomy, personal site, Media Lab alumni) corroborate MIT/Media Lab path and later DIVA/Post/Plum/Nokia/Google X career. Family background largely undocumented; MIT–Apple–Media Lab pipeline is the clearest early advantage.
starting_point: Born 1962 in Waterville, Maine; raised in Norway near Hønefoss; public schools and Norwegian military before MIT computer science.
current_position: Former Google/X VP and head of Everyday Robots; public speaker, advisor, and writer on AI/robotics and technology entrepreneurship.

trajectory.event: Co-founded Snappy Software with Apple seed funding after MIT undergrad; early expert-systems startup.
Joined Apple Computer to work on HyperCard development from Japan.
Co-founded DIVA (Digital Video Applications), first commercial Media Lab spin-off; VideoShop later acquired by Avid (1993).
Founded Post Communications, customized email marketing; later sold to Netcentives.
Founded Plum Ventures social network for small groups; acquired by Nokia mapping division in 2009.
Joined Google X as VP to reorganize robotics; led Everyday Robots moonshot.

CS pipeline and multi-year platform practice are clear; family financial advantage not documented. Material creator milestone by 26 is the breakout video plus subsequent full-time creator transition.
starting_point: Born 1992 in Gainesville, Florida; mother died in childhood; attended Eastside High IB then Georgia Tech computer science.
current_position: Full-time YouTuber and podcaster (Sad Boyz) with multi-million combined subscribers; former Patreon engineering manager; San Francisco–based creator.

trajectory.event: Created YouTube channel (later VSympathyV / Jarvis Johnson) while still in high school.
Graduated Georgia Tech BS CS with high honors; entered software engineering (Google practicum, Yelp, later Patreon).
August breakout 5-Minute Crafts commentary video; transitioned toward full-time YouTube career.
